extracted.intended_audience: participants and representatives in Copyright Claims Board (CCB) proceedings (claimants, respondents, legal counsel, authorized representatives, law firms, solo practitioners, law students, pro bono clinics)
extracted.subtask_short: CCB participant conduct and filing limits
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules governing participant conduct, representations to the Board, sanctions for bad-faith conduct, requirements and duties for legal counsel/authorized representatives, and numerical and temporary limits on CCB filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant conduct: respect, ethics, and truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants shall act with the utmost respect for others and shall behave ethically and truthfully in connection with all submissions and appearances before the Copyright Claims Board (Board). (§232.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all parties including legal counsel and authorized representatives; establishes baseline expectation of professional and truthful behavior in CCB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations to the Board: certification standard
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting materials or advocating positions before the Board, a participant certifies that, to the best of the participant's knowledge, information, and belief, formed after a reasonable inquiry under the circumstances: (a) not presented for any improper purpose; (b) legal contentions are made in good faith based on reasonable understanding of existing law; (c) factual contentions have evidentiary support or, if identified, will likely have evidentiary support after reasonable investigation/discovery; (d) denials of factual contentions have evidentiary support or are reasonably based on belief or lack of information. (§232.2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires reasonable inquiry before filing; covers improper purpose, legal and factual assertions, and denials. Failure to meet this certification can trigger sanctions under bad-faith rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad-faith conduct: fee/costs award obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall award costs and attorneys' fees as part of a determination where it is established that a participant engaged in bad-faith conduct, unless such an award would be inconsistent with the interests of justice. (§232.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that findings of bad-faith can carry monetary sanctions; award is discretionary if inconsistent with interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad-faith procedure — Board-initiated allegations (show cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: On its own, and prior to a final determination, the Board may order a participant to show cause why certain conduct does not constitute bad-faith conduct. The accused participant shall file a response within 14 days following procedures in §220.5(a)(2). (§232.3(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may act sua sponte; strict 14-day response timeframe and specified procedural form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad-faith procedure — party-initiated allegations (conference request)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that in good faith believes a participant has engaged in bad-faith conduct may file a request for a conference with the Board describing the alleged conduct and attaching relevant exhibits; such requests and responses follow §220.5(a)(2). (§232.3(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables parties to initiate review of alleged bad-faith; procedural requirements for content and exhibits; follows existing conference/request procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing bad-faith: determination or conference
rubrics_metrics.description: After the accused participant's response has been filed or the time to file has passed, the Board shall either determine that no bad-faith occurred or schedule a conference concerning the allegations. (§232.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes next-step outcomes after response — either dismissal of allegations or proceeding to conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining awards for bad-faith: factors and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether to award attorneys' fees and costs due to bad-faith conduct, and the amount, the Board shall consider the requests and responses submitted, any arguments on the issue, and the accused participant's behavior in other Board proceedings. Award shall be limited to not more than $5,000, unless (1) adversely affected party appeared pro se (limit $2,500) or (2) extraordinary circumstances (pattern/practice) allow award in excess. (§232.3(d))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies factors Board must consider and sets statutory caps with limited exceptions for extraordinary circumstances or pro se respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar on initiating/participating after multiple bad-faith findings
rubrics_metrics.description: A participant found to have engaged in bad-faith conduct on more than one occasion within a 12-month period shall be subject to penalties including potential bar from initiating claims or, for counsel/authorized representatives, from participating on a party's behalf. (§232.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates consequence of repeated bad-faith behavior within a 12-month window; triggers additional sanctions beyond fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for alleging multiple instances of bad-faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Board may order a participant to show cause regarding conduct on more than one occasion within 12 months (14-day response per §220.5(a)(2)). A party may request a conference describing alleged instances and attaching exhibits, including CCB case numbers if known; a respondent's request before opt-out does not waive opt-out right. (§232.4(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels single-incident procedures but requires details of multiple instances; protects respondents' opt-out rights when they file such requests early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing a pattern of bad-faith conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: After response or time lapse, the Board will determine whether the participant has engaged in bad-faith on more than one occasion within 12 months or schedule a conference. An award of attorneys' fees or costs under §232.3 within the prior 12 months establishes an instance; Board may consider other evidence of bad-faith that did not result in an award, including claims found noncompliant or where respondent opted out. (§232.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that prior fee awards are dispositive instances and that other non-award evidence may be considered when establishing a pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for pattern of bad-faith conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board finds bad-faith conduct on more than one occasion within 12 months, the written determination shall include (1) bar from initiating claims or, for counsel/representatives, bar from participating for 12 months; (2) in party pattern, dismissal without prejudice of proceedings commenced by that claimant/respondent/representative that are still pending (active proceeding dismissed only with respondent's written consent); (3) in counsel/representative pattern, bar from representing any party before the Board for 12 months; Board may consider hardship to parties and may amend scheduling orders or issue stays to allow new representation. (§232.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details specific remedial actions the Board will include in written determinations and the Board's discretion to mitigate hardship caused by counsel bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of appearance and eCCB account linking
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party elects representation, legal counsel or authorized representative (other than counsel who filed the claim) must file a request to link their eCCB user account to the case and to the party they represent; the account must contain bar number (if applicable), mailing address, email, and telephone number. To withdraw, file a Request to Withdraw Representation. (§232.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative requirement to formally link counsel/rep accounts and provide accurate contact and bar information; separate process for withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar admissions requirement for legal counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal counsel must be a member in good standing of the bar of the highest court of a State, D.C., or any territory/commonwealth of the U.S. Law student representation must qualify under part 234. Counsel/representative must file a written statement under penalty of perjury that they are currently qualified and authorized to represent the party. (§232.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes eligibility to practice before the Board and requires sworn certification of qualification; distinguishes law students per separate rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbarred counsel prohibition and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Any legal counsel disbarred by any Federal court, State court, D.C., or any territory/commonwealth shall not be allowed to represent a party before the Board. If counsel in any active or pending proceeding is disbarred, they must report the disbarment to the Board and withdraw representation. (§232.5(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute bar on representation by disbarred attorneys and affirmative reporting/withdrawal requirement upon disbarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of legal counsel/authorized representatives (candor, impartiality, fairness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal counsel or authorized representative has a duty of candor and impartiality toward the Board, and a duty of fairness toward opposing parties. The Board will consider the rules of professional conduct of D.C. and the State in which counsel practices when assessing breaches. (§232.5(d))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies ethical duties and identifies applicable professional conduct rules as assessment benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for counsel/representative misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Any legal counsel or authorized representative found to be in violation of the rules of conduct in this section, or otherwise behaving unethically or inappropriately before the Board, may be barred from representing parties in proceedings before the Board for a period of twelve months. (§232.5(e))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides explicit 12-month bar remedy for counsel misconduct; parallels participant-pattern penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum number of proceedings per claimant and counsel in 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical caps on filings in any 12-month period: (1) a claimant (including corporate parents, subsidiaries, affiliates) shall file no more than 30 proceedings; (2) a sole practitioner shall file no more than 40 CCB proceedings on behalf of claimants; (3) a law firm shall file no more than 80 CCB proceedings on behalf of claimants. A proceeding counts toward the limit as soon as it is filed regardless of resolution. Amendments or counterclaims do not count as additional claims. (§233.2(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines numeric filing limits, what counts as a proceeding, and clarifies that resolution, dismissal, noncompliance, opt-out, or amendments/counterclaims do not increase the tally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumvention of filing limits and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claimant files in excess of the limitation, the claim shall be dismissed without prejudice. If a sole practitioner or counsel associated with a law firm files in excess, the counsel or law firm shall be ordered to withdraw and the Board may stay the proceeding for 60 days (extendable for good cause) for the claimant to retain new counsel. Taking action solely to avoid the limit may be considered bad-faith conduct under §232.3. (§233.2(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides remedial steps for excess filings and warns that evasion may trigger bad-faith sanctions; stay period to obtain new counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception to filing limits for law students/clinics/pro bono
rubrics_metrics.description: The numerical limitations do not apply to law students or a law clinic or pro bono legal services organization with a connection to the participating law student's law school. (§233.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carves out exemption for supervised student and certain pro bono representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary moratorium on new claims when capacity overwhelmed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board determines pending cases have overwhelmed its capacity, it may impose a temporary stay on the filing of claims, publishing an announcement on its website stating the effective date and duration of the stay, not to exceed six months. (§233.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative tool to manage docket; public notice requirement and six-month maximum duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception to moratorium when statute of limitations will expire
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claimant's statute of limitations under 17 U.S.C. 1504(b) is about to expire during a stay, the claimant may file on or before the statutory deadline with a declaration under penalty of perjury stating the statute will expire during the stay and facts in support. If the Board determines the statute likely will expire, it will hold the claim in abeyance and conduct a compliance review after the stay. (§233.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits narrow filing despite moratorium with sworn facts; Board discretion to hold claim in abeyance and later review compliance.
